name: Gupchup
instructions: 1. Knead suji and maida with water into a stiff dough, roll into tiny circles, and deep-fry until golden and crisp.
2. Prepare the filling by mashing boiled potatoes with boiled chickpeas, chopped green chilies, coriander, salt, and roasted cumin powder.
3. Create the 'pani' (spiced water) by blending tamarind pulp, mint, ginger, green chilies, water, black salt, and chaat masala.
4. To serve, poke a hole in the center of a puri, add a spoonful of the potato mixture, and dip it into the spicy tamarind water before consuming immediately.
description: Gupchup is the beloved Odia version of panipuri. It holds immense cultural significance in Odisha as a quintessential street food, often enjoyed in the evenings at roadside stalls where the vendor serves them one by one, creating a unique social experience.
